catalog_quote: Le ton en wüödughukakan n’a pas été objet d’une analyse approfondie. Tous ceux qui ont débuté une analyse tonale du worodugukakan constatent que le ton joue un rôle distinctif au niveau lexical, et qu’il a en plus de cela une fonction grammaticale.21 Au niveau appliqué de l‘orthographe, nous avons observé que les orateurs n'ont jamais eu de difficulté à lire un texte ou à comprendre un texte lu à voix haute pendant les ateliers. C’est cela qui justifie de ne pas écrire le ton dans l’orthographe. [fn. 21: Gingiss (1973 : 42); Derive (1983 : 304); Boling : courriel du 30 mai 2016] ... [p.44:] Cette unité prosodique est le pied phonologique. En mandé, la notion de pied phonologique n’est pas liée à l’idée d’inégalité de syllabes (c.-à.-d. syllabes accentuées vs syllabes non accentuées), mais à l’idée d’une interdépendance des segments à l’intérieur du pied.41
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

[p.44:] En mandé, la notion de pied phonologique n’est pas liée à l’idée d’inégalité de syllabes (c.-à.-d. syllabes accentuées vs syllabes non accentuées), mais à l’idée d’une interdépendance des segments à l’intérieur du pied.
new_statements.translation: Tone in Wüödughukakan has not been the object of an in-depth analysis. All who have begun a tonal analysis of Worodugukakan find that tone plays a distinctive role at the lexical level and that it additionally has a grammatical function. [fn: Gingiss 1973:42; Derive 1983:304; Boling p.c.] At the applied level of the orthography, we observed that speakers never had difficulty reading a text or understanding a text read aloud during the workshops. This is what justifies not writing tone in the orthography. [p.44:] In Mande, the notion of phonological foot is not tied to the idea of inequality among syllables (i.e. stressed vs unstressed syllables) but to the idea of an interdependence of the segments inside the foot.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Worodugukakan is described as a tone language (lexically and grammatically distinctive tone, at least H vs L; Derive 1985 adds a further high register in nominals). None of the accessible descriptions says anything about word stress or a word accent; the only accent-related remark is the borrowed general-Mande statement that the disyllabic phonological foot is defined by segmental interdependence, not by stressed vs unstressed syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: None; authors explicitly say tone has not been analysed in depth.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical/grammatical tone at word level and orthography practice; the foot remark (p.44) is quoted from Kuznetsova 2007 / Vydrine 2003 about Mande generally and applied by Blecke to Worodugukakan word structure, not an independent claim about stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Blecke 2019 describes wüödughukakan as spoken around Séguéla (reference villages Soba-Banandjé and Béréni-Dialla; 'petites nuances dialectales' only), i.e. woro1256 proper. Creissels 1988, also examined, describes Koyaga of Mankono, a neighbouring Manding lect with its own glottocode (koya1253, ISO kga) — not woro1256. Derive 1985 treats worodugukakan as one of four Ivorian Manding lects.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. §2.5 p.22: tone is lexically distinctive and has grammatical function, not analysed in depth, not. Appendix 2 p.44 quotes the general-Mande view that the phonological foot is not about stressed vs unstressed syllables (Kuznetsova 2007, Vydrine 2003).
